hook_text: Physics isn't about guessing. It's about predicting the world mathematically.
clip_script:
[00:00:00] Grandmaster: Physics is not merely about observing the world; it is about predicting it with absolute precision. 
[00:00:05] Grandmaster: Sir Isaac Newton provided us with the formal mathematical framework to do exactly that. 
[00:00:10] Grandmaster: When a net force acts on an object, the object will accelerate in the direction of the net force.
[00:00:16] Grandmaster: If I apply a greater net force to the same object, the acceleration increases. That is the direct proportionality.
[00:00:24] Grandmaster: The equation F_net = m · a is not merely a suggestion; it is a rigid, mathematical truth that governs the macroscopic universe.
[00:00:32] Grandmaster: Consider a 5 kg crate pulled by a 20 N force.
[00:00:37] Grandmaster: Formula. Substitution. Answer with units. F_net = m · a.
[00:00:43] Grandmaster: 20 equals 5 times a. Therefore, a is 4 meters per second squared.
[00:00:49] Grandmaster: This is the only acceptable method. It is logical, traceable, and undeniably correct.
[00:00:56] Grandmaster: The universe operates on rules, and we have just mastered one of them.
